title: CRLR/56/2017 of Smt. Rainu AND ANOTHER Vs Anuj

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No.56 of 2017
Smt. Rainu & Anr.
 .Ö Revisionists
Versus
Anuj
 Ö.. Respondent
Mr. M.S. Tyagi, Advocate for the revisionists
Mr. S.P. Singh, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Sanjeev Singh, Advocate for the
respondent
Dated: 07.09.2018
Honíble Lok Pal Singh, J.
 This criminal revision is directed against the
judgment and order dated 01.03.2017 passed by
Additional Judge, Family Court, Roorkee, District
Haridwar in case no.167 of 2014, whereby said court
has partly allowed the application moved by the
revisionists under Section 125 of The Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973 and has directed the respondent to
pay ` 1,000/- each to revisionist no.1 and revisionist
no.2, in total ` 2,000/- per month, as maintenance
allowance, from the date of institution of the suit.
2. In nutshell, the facts of the case are that the
revisionist no.1 moved an application under Section
125 of Cr.P.C. stating therein that revisionist no.1/wife
got married to the respondent as per Hindu rituals on
25.04.2012. In the marriage, dowry was given to the
respondent, however, the respondent and his family
members were not happy with the marriage and they
started torturing her for bringing insufficient dowry.

2
On 12.04.2013, a girl child (revisionist no.2) was born
out of the wedlock. She alleged that entire expenses
were borne by her parents in the hospital. When the
revisionist no.1 came to her matrimonial house, the
respondent again made demand of dowry and
thereafter left her to her parental house. In this regard,
a Panchayat was called on 23.09.2013 wherein the
respondent and his family members outrightly refused
to take revisionist to their house without any dowry.
Revisionist/wife alleged that she has no source of
income and she is unable to maintain herself and her
children, whereas on the other hand, respondent has
40-45 Bighas of land, out of which in 30 Bigha land
there is mango orchard, from where there is earning of
`3,00,000/- annually. Besides this, the respondent is
working in a medicine company from where also he is
getting `12,000/- per month. Thus, the revisionists
moved the application u/s 125 Cr.P.C. and claimed a
sum of `10,000/- as monthly maintenance allowance
from the respondent.
3. The respondent filed objections to the
application. In his objections, he admitted the factum
of marriage and also the fact that a girl child was born
out of their wedlock, but denied the remaining
allegations made in the application. He also alleged
that the revisionist/wife is living separately without
any cause; she is a graduate and she is working in
Titan Company from where she is getting salary @
`8,000/- per month.
4. In support of the contents of the application,
the revisionist/wife got examined herself as PW1. In

3
oral evidence, respondent got examined himself as
DW1. The trial court, after hearing the parties and
upon perusal of entire evidence, directed as above.
Hence, present revision has been filed by the
revisionists for seeking enhancement in the amount of
maintenance to the tune of `10,000/-
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties
and have perused the entire record.
6. The contention of the revisionist/wife is that
she has no sufficient means to maintain herself and
her child, whereas the respondent/husband is working
in a medicine company and also has 40-45 Bighas of
land. In support of her case, revisionist no.1 filed her
statement in the form of affidavit wherein she
specifically stated that the respondent is working in Ski
Mat Medicine Company from where he is getting `
12,000/- per month. However, in cross-examination,
the respondent denied to the suggestion that he is
working in Ski Mat medicine company. He stated that
he is doing labour work. The trial court, in the absence
of any documentary evidence in support of the income
of the respondent, has awarded maintenance to the
tune of Rs.1,000/- each to wife and child, but while
doing so, the trial court has lost sight of the fact that
copy of statement of the respondent recorded in a misc.
case no.3/14 under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C. was filed
by the revisionist no.1, which was also taken on record
in the trial court wherein the respondent Anuj has
deposed that he is working in a medicine company.

4
7. It is not disputed that the revisionist no.1 is
legally wedded wife of the respondent. It is also not
disputed that the revisionist no.2 has born out of the
wedlock. Thus, it is the duty of the
husband/respondent to maintain his legally wedded
wife and minor child. It is common knowledge that
prices of the essential commodities are increasing day
by day. Furthermore, maintenance also does not mean
only a provision for food, clothing and lodging but it
provides that there must be a proper provision for
education of the children also. This being the position,
the judgment of the trial court requires interference
and modification. Considering the entire conspectus of
things, an amount of ` 3,000/- per month to revisionist
no.1/wife and ` 3,000/- per month to revisionist no.2
would serve the ends of justice in the present case.
8. Accordingly, the revision is partly allowed.
Impugned judgment and order dated 01.03.2017
passed by Additional Judge, Family Court, Roorkee,
District Haridwar in misc. case no.167 of 2014, is
modified and it is directed that the respondent shall
pay `3,000/- per month to revisionist no.1/wife and
`3,000/- to revisionist no.2/child, in total `6,000/- per
month, from the date of institution of case.
9. No order as to costs.
(Lok Pal Singh, J.)
 07.09.2018
Rajni
